Karthik / Elaine — looping in a short technical note to set expectations from the performance side before the pilot: 

- Warmup behavior: for replayed traffic we need a warmup period to populate KV caches and transformer caches. Pilot should include a 15–30 minute warmup segment (low-rate) before the full-duration replay.
- Suggested sizing (initial): for a peak of ~4.5k QPS with 6k spikes, recommend starting capacity equivalent to 3 medium GPU nodes (we map these to 'dedicated-small' in our quote) with autoscale + 1 reserve node. This gives headroom for spikes and KV warmup. If customer prefers single-shot cost-sensitive run, we can propose a 2-node baseline with tighter throttles but risk higher latency on spikes.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p99 latency, token cost, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit ratio, and sequence-length distribution. Recommend we capture a small set of timed traces for the 1% pilot to validate kernel selection.

Dependencies: access to the replay payload + a mapping file that ties requests to expected session ids (helps us validate correctness). Also confirm whether StormTech wants us to run the replay from Redwood-hosted infra (we can do it) or they prefer to pull and run in their staging (ops-runbook-template.md attached).

I'll prepare a short capacity worksheet after we see the pilot sample (Marissa).

—Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
